mainTopic: דחוי of קרבנות, and the search for בן עזאי's source that an עולה שלא לשמה is פסול
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a list of lessons from the previous page: דחוי applies even to something holy only for its money value. רבי יוחנן then rules that if someone set aside a קרבן for eating חלב and then became a משומד or a שוטה, the קרבן stays rejected even after he becomes fit again: הואיל ונדחה ידחה. The גמרא explains why both rulings were needed. רבי ירמיה asks about a בית דין that permitted the חלב and then reversed itself. An elder answers that this is the clearest case of all, because the קרבן itself was pushed away. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, explains why שמעון בן עזאי speaks of 'seventy-two זָקֵן' in the singular, and searches for his source that an עולה brought שלא לשמה is פסול. It tries the word 'הוּא', then a קל וחומר from חטאת, then a הצד השוה from חטאת and פסח, and each attempt is challenged. The answer, which begins with בן עזאי's name, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rejection applies even to money-value holiness
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a list of lessons: דחוי applies even to קדשת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is rejection even with things that are holy for their monetary value.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a list of lessons that the גמרא learned from a statement on the previous page. It says that דחוי (permanent rejection) applies even to something that is holy only for its money value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some holy things are holy in their very body (קדושת הגוף). Others are holy only for their value (קדושת דמים). You might think דחוי only works on the stronger kind of holiness, but this line says it works even on the weaker kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejection: a קרבן is pushed off and can never be brought again
Literally 'money'; here it means holiness that applies to an item's monetary value
Holiness of the body itself, the stronger kind of holiness

steps.whatToRemember: דחוי is not limited to things holy in their body. Even קדושת דמים can be permanently rejected.

phrases.english: There is rejection with monetary value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of lessons from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דחוי applies even to קדושת דמים.

steps.title: The owner became a משומד and then returned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: if the owner of a קרבן became a משומד and then did תשובה, the קרבן stays rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate חלב, set aside a קרבן, then became a משומד, and later returned, the קרבן was already pushed off, so it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא reports a ruling of רבי יוחנן. A person set aside a קרבן for eating חלב and then became a משומד, who cannot bring a קרבן. Even after he comes back, his קרבן stays rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is הואיל ונדחה ידחה: once the קרבן could not be brought, that rejection is permanent. Becoming fit again later does not bring the קרבן back.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
He set aside an animal as his קרבן
He became a משומד, one who abandoned Torah observance
He changed his mind and came back
Since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the main rule of the section. A temporary problem with the owner can make his קרבן rejected forever.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and he became an apostate, and then he recanted,
since it was rejected, it stays rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling on the theme of דחוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner of a קרבן becomes a משומד and later returns, his קרבן remains permanently rejected.

steps.title: The owner became a שוטה and then recovered
steps.stepSummary: A second ruling of רבי יוחנן: if the owner became a שוטה and then recovered, the קרבן also stays rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said, by רבי ירמיה in the name of רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate חלב, set aside a קרבן, then became a שוטה, and later became sane again, the קרבן was already pushed off, so it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of רבי יוחנן with the same rule, הואיל ונדחה ידחה. This time the owner lost his sanity and then got it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוטה cannot bring a קרבן, so while he was insane the קרבן was pushed off. Even though he recovers, the rejection stays. The case changes, but the rule is the same as in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (another report on the same subject)
He became a שוטה, mentally incompetent
He became sane again

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Abbahu said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and he became insane, and then became sane again,
since it was rejected, it stays rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling of the same רבי יוחנן with a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner of a קרבן becomes a שוטה and later recovers, his קרבן remains permanently rejected.

steps.title: Why both rulings are needed: the first side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why we need both rulings. From the משומד case alone we might think the rejection applies only to one who disqualified himself by his own action; the שוטה, who was disqualified by itself (not through his own action), would be like someone sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If we had only been taught the first case, we would say the rejection is because he pushed himself away with his own actions. But here, where he was pushed off by itself, he is like someone who is asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: why did רבי יוחנן need to teach both cases? It starts with one side: the משומד case alone would not teach us the שוטה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משומד made himself unfit by his own choice, so it makes sense to punish him with דחוי. The שוטה became unfit without choosing it, so we might compare him to a sleeping person, whose קרבן is surely not rejected. The second ruling is needed to tell us that even the שוטה's קרבן is rejected. The other side of the explanation continues after this.

keyTerms.meaning: And they are needed (both statements are necessary)
Literally 'with hands': by his own action
By itself, without his doing
He is like a sleeping person

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison to a sleeping person is what we WOULD have thought from the first case alone. It is not the final ruling, because רבי יוחנן ruled that the שוטה's קרבן is rejected.

phrases.english: And both are necessary;
for if he had taught us only the first one,
phrases.notes: The first one is the משומד case from step 2.

phrases.english: we would say it is because he pushed himself away by his own action;
but here, where he was pushed off by itself,
he is like one who is asleep.
phrases.notes: Someone who falls asleep after setting aside his קרבן obviously doesn't lose it; that's the comparison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the two rulings in steps 2 and 3 do not repeat each other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי יוחנן need to teach both the משומד case and the שוטה case?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משומד case alone would not cover the שוטה, since the שוטה became unfit by himself and might be compared to a sleeping person. The reverse side continues after this.

steps.title: Why the משומד ruling is needed too
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן had taught only the שוטה case, we might think the משומד is different, because he can do תשובה whenever he wants. So both rulings are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only the שוטה case, we would say the קרבן stays rejected there because the שוטה cannot fix himself. But a משומד can fix himself whenever he chooses, so I might say his קרבן is not rejected forever. That is why both rulings are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the 'why do we need both rulings' explanation from step 4. It shows that the שוטה ruling alone would not teach us the משומד case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that the משומד case could not teach the שוטה case. This step shows the reverse. A שוטה has no power to recover, so his loss of fitness looks more serious. A משומד can do תשובה at any moment, so we might think his קרבן was never truly pushed away. Because each case has its own possible way out, רבי יוחנן had to teach both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in his power to return (to being fit)
It is in his power to return (he can do תשובה any time)
It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
I would say not

steps.whatToRemember: Each case teaches something the other cannot. The משומד was able to fix himself, and the שוטה was not, yet in both cases the קרבן stays דחוי.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only here
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the שוטה case, someone who lost his sanity.

phrases.english: [I would say it is rejected] because it is not in his power to return;
but here, where it is in his power to return,
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the משומד, who can do תשובה whenever he wants.

phrases.english: I would say it is not [rejected]. Therefore it is necessary [to teach both].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא begun in step 4 by giving the other side of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן needed to say both rulings.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שוטה case alone could not teach the משומד case, because the משומד can return by choice. So both rulings are needed.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about a reversed בית דין ruling
steps.stepSummary: Someone ate חלב and set aside a קרבן. Then בית דין ruled that this חלב was permitted, and later they took the ruling back. Is the קרבן דחוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: A person ate חלב and set aside a קרבן for it. Then בית דין ruled that this חלב is allowed. Later they took back their ruling. What is the law? Is the קרבן rejected forever or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה raises a new question, a בעיא, about a different way a קרבן might become דחוי. This time the cause is a ruling of בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While בית דין's ruling was in force, the person seemed to have no sin, so his קרבן had no purpose. Once the ruling was reversed, the קרבן is needed again. The question is whether that period of not being needed makes the קרבן דחוי forever.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised an open question, a בעיא)
Forbidden fat; eating it by mistake requires a חטאת
He set aside an animal as a קרבן
The court gave a ruling
They took back (reversed) their ruling

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering [for it],
and the court ruled that [this] fat is permitted,
and then they took back [their ruling], what is [the law]?

phrases.aramaic: מִי הָוֵי דָּחוּי, אוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי?
phrases.english: Is it rejected, or is it not rejected?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוחנן's cases, where the owner became unfit, to a new case where a court ruling made the קרבן unneeded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a קרבן become permanently דחוי when בית דין's mistaken permission made it unneeded for a while?

steps.title: The elder: this is the most obvious case of דחוי
steps.stepSummary: An elder says that רבי יוחנן opened his teaching on דחויין with exactly this case. In the earlier cases only the person was pushed away, but here the קרבן itself was pushed away.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: When רבי יוחנן began teaching about rejected offerings, he began with this case. Why? In those cases the man was rejected, not the קרבן. Here the קרבן itself was rejected too.
steps.whatsHappening: An elder answers רבי ירמיה: yes, the קרבן is דחוי. In fact, this was רבי יוחנן's very first and clearest example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the משומד and the שוטה, the animal was still a perfectly good קרבן; only its owner had become unfit. In רבי ירמיה's case, the ruling of בית דין took away the קרבן's whole purpose, so the קרבן itself was pushed away. If דחוי applies even when only the person was pushed away, it surely applies here.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder (a wise old man whose name is not given)
He opened (began his teaching)
Rejected offerings
The man was pushed away
Was pushed away (rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the elder is saying this case is less clear. He means the opposite: this is the strongest case of דחוי, because the קרבן itself lost its purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of being pushed away: the owner (משומד, שוטה) or the קרבן itself (the בית דין case). The second is the stronger case of דחוי.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
When Rabbi Yochanan began [teaching] about rejected offerings,
he began with this [case].
What is the reason?
There, the man was pushed away,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משומד and שוטה cases from steps 2 and 3.

phrases.english: [but] the offering was not pushed away;
here, the offering itself was also pushed away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the קרבן דחוי after the reversed ruling?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. This is רבי יוחנן's first and most obvious case, because the קרבן itself was pushed away and not only its owner.

steps.title: Quoting שמעון בן עזאי from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes שמעון בן עזאי, who received a tradition from seventy-two elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן עזאי said: I received a tradition from seventy-two elders, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the words of שמעון בן עזאי. It is setting up a question about his exact wording, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, שמעון בן עזאי reports a tradition about offerings slaughtered for the wrong purpose. The גמרא quotes only his opening words, and the 'כו׳' (etc.) stands for the rest. Its interest here is one word: 'זָקֵן'.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received a tradition
Elder (singular form)
Etc.: the rest of the quoted text is left out

phrases.english: Shimon ben Azzai said:

phrases.aramaic: מְקוּבְּלַנִי מִפִּי שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זָקֵן כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: I received [a tradition] from the mouth of seventy-two elder, etc.
phrases.notes: The word for 'elder' here is singular. That odd wording is exactly what the גמרא asks about next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי מְקוּבְּלַנִי מִפִּי שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of דחוי and returns to a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון בן עזאי reports a tradition he received from seventy-two elders.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'elder' and not 'elders'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה uses the singular word 'זָקֵן' together with the number seventy-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he need to say 'seventy-two elder' (singular)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the unusual wording in the משנה. With a number like seventy-two, we would expect the plural 'זְקֵנִים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question about wording, not about a law. The גמרא assumes the singular form was chosen on purpose to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need to teach (this wording)?
Elders (the plural form we would expect)

phrases.english: Why do I need to teach
"seventy-two elder" [in the singular]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the line quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the singular 'זָקֵן' is used with a plural number.

steps.title: They all held one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The singular form shows that all seventy-two elders agreed. They spoke as if with one voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because all of them stood together in one line of thinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the singular word shows the seventy-two elders were completely united on this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The singular 'זָקֵן' presents the whole group as one unit. This tells us there was no disagreement among them. That makes שמעון בן עזאי's tradition stronger, because it comes from a united group.

keyTerms.meaning: In one line (one shared opinion)
They stood (held that position)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Seventy-two זָקֵן' is singular because all the elders agreed as one.

phrases.english: Because all of them, in one line [of opinion],
were standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All seventy-two elders held one opinion, so they are spoken of as one.

steps.title: בן עזאי adds only the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends the tradition of בן עזאי: the only offering he adds to the list is the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי added nothing except the עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. בן עזאי's tradition adds one more offering, the עולה, to the list of offerings that are פסול when brought שלא לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה said only the פסח and the חטאת become פסול when brought שלא לשמה. בן עזאי's tradition adds the עולה to that short list, and nothing else. This sets up the next question: what is his source?

keyTerms.meaning: Added (to the list)
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Not for its own sake, brought with the wrong offering in mind

steps.confusionAlert: 'Added' does not mean the עולה is added to the regular rule. It means the עולה joins the פסח and the חטאת as offerings that become פסול when brought שלא לשמה.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai did not add
phrases.notes: Added to the list from the first משנה: the פסח and the חטאת, which are פסול when brought שלא לשמה.

phrases.english: anything except the burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הוֹסִיף בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of בן עזאי's tradition from the seventy-two elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה brought שלא לשמה is פסול, like the פסח and the חטאת.

steps.title: רב הונא gives the source: the word 'it' by the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that בן עזאי learns from the word 'הוּא' in the פסוק about the עולה: only 'it', meaning brought as an עולה, is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is בן עזאי's reason? The פסוק says 'It is an עולה, a fire offering of pleasing aroma to ה''. 'It' means: brought for its own sake, it is כשר. Brought not for its own sake, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks for בן עזאי's source and answers it himself. The source is the word 'הוּא' ('it') in the פסוק about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוּא' seems extra, so it is read as a limit. The offering is only an acceptable 'pleasing aroma' when it is brought as itself, an עולה. If it is brought with a different offering in mind, it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asking for a source)
A fire offering
A pleasing aroma
Valid
Invalid, disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the pattern used in the rest of the discussion: the word 'הוּא' can show that an offering must be brought לשמה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
What is the reason of Ben Azzai?
"It is a burnt offering, a fire offering
of pleasing aroma to the Lord" –
"it": for its own sake, it is valid;
not for its own sake, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind בן עזאי's ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'הוּא' by the עולה teaches that it is פסול when brought שלא לשמה.

steps.title: But the guilt offering also has the word 'it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: the word 'הוּא' is also written by the אשם, yet an אשם brought שלא לשמה is not פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'it' is also written about the אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's source. If 'הוּא' makes an offering פסול when brought שלא לשמה, the אשם should be פסול too, since it also has the word 'הוּא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'אשם הוּא', using the same word. But neither the first משנה nor בן עזאי counts the אשם among the offerings that become פסול. So either the source is wrong, or the אשם needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Also
It is written about it

phrases.english: A guilt offering also
has "it" written about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the word 'הוּא' makes an offering פסול when brought שלא לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by the אשם, yet an אשם brought שלא לשמה is not פסול. So the word alone cannot prove the rule.

steps.title: By the guilt offering, 'it' refers to the burning of the portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by the אשם, 'הוּא' is written after the burning of the אימורים, a stage that does not hold back the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is written after the burning of the אימורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. By the אשם, the word 'הוּא' is written about the burning of the אימורים on the מזבח, not about the main service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם is כשר even if its אימורים are never burned at all. So if they are burned שלא לשמה, it is surely still כשר. The 'הוּא' by the אשם cannot teach a פסול, while the 'הוּא' by the עולה can, and רב הונא's source stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the sacrificial portions (fats and organs) on the מזבח
After
That one (that פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the 'הוּא' by the אשם is set aside because it is written about the burning of the אימורים, and an אשם is כשר even without that burning. The next step turns this same answer against the עולה.

phrases.english: That one is after
the burning of the sacrificial portions
that it is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לְאַחַר הַקְטָרַת אֵימוּרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and protects רב הונא's source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the context of the word: by the אשם it describes a stage that does not hold back the offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'הוּא' by the אשם should make it פסול שלא לשמה, just like the עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: By the אשם, 'הוּא' refers to burning the אימורים, which is not essential, so it teaches no פסול. Step 15 immediately challenges this.

steps.title: The עולה's 'הוּא' also comes after the burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the previous answer back on רב הונא: the 'הוּא' by the עולה is also written after the burning of the אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this 'הוּא' by the עולה is also written after the burning of the אימורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave in Step 14. That answer is a problem for the עולה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the אשם's 'הוּא' doesn't count because it comes after the burning, which is not a step that holds back the offering. But the עולה's 'הוּא' is also placed after the burning. So by that same logic, it should not teach anything about the שחיטה either.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
That is written
The parts of the animal burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: This one too, after the burning of the sacrificial portions,
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the 'הוּא' written by the עולה, which רב הונא relied on.

phrases.english: is where it is written!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נָמֵי לְאַחַר הַקְטָרַת אֵימוּרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of the Step 14 answer against רב הונא's own source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's derivation from 'הוּא' by the עולה, as defended in Step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a 'הוּא' after the burning does not hold back the offering by the אשם, the same should be true by the עולה.

steps.title: The עולה has two 'הוּא's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by the עולה, 'הוּא' is written twice, so the extra one can teach about the main שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two 'הוּא's are written by the עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. The עולה has the word 'הוּא' twice, not once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'הוּא' covers the burning. The second one is extra, so it can be used to teach that the main service must be done for the sake of an עולה. That is why only the עולה becomes פסול שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written

phrases.english: Two instances of 'it' are written.
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 1:13 and שמות 29:18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק: a second 'הוּא' frees one up to teach about the main service
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולה's 'הוּא' is only after the burning, so it teaches nothing about שחיטה
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה has a second, extra 'הוּא' that does teach about the main service

steps.title: The אשם also has two 'הוּא's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the אשם also has 'הוּא' written twice, yet it is not פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: By the אשם too, two 'הוּא's are written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the 'two הוּא's' answer. The אשם has two as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two 'הוּא's are what make the עולה פסול שלא לשמה, the אשם should be פסול too. But it isn't. So counting 'הוּא's cannot explain בן עזאי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to, by

phrases.english: With regard to a guilt offering as well,
two instances of 'it' are written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 16 by showing the אשם has the same feature.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that two 'הוּא's set the עולה apart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשם also has two 'הוּא's, yet an אשם brought שלא לשמה is כשר. So the number of 'הוּא's cannot be the reason.

steps.title: בן עזאי learns his rule from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'הוּא' approach. It says בן עזאי learns from a קל וחומר: if a חטאת, which is not fully burned, is פסול שלא לשמה, then surely an עולה, which is fully burned, is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, בן עזאי learns it from a קל וחומר. A חטאת is not fully burned, and still, if one slaughtered it not for its sake, it is פסול. An עולה is fully burned, so all the more so it should be פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on learning בן עזאי's rule from the word 'הוּא'. It offers a new source: a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a חטאת slaughtered שלא לשמה is פסול. A חטאת is partly eaten by כהנים, while an עולה goes completely on the מזבח, which makes it the stricter offering. If the lighter offering is פסול, the stricter one must be פסול too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier idea)
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
He derives it
Fully burned on the מזבח
Is it not all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא drops the 'הוּא' source and tries a קל וחומר from חטאת instead. The next step challenges this קל וחומר too.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אלא' means the גמרא is giving up on רב הונא's 'הוּא' explanation. It is not adding a second proof alongside it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the back-and-forth over רב הונא's 'הוּא' source and starts a new line of reasoning, the קל וחומר, which the following steps test.

phrases.english: Rather, ben Azzai
derives it through an a fortiori inference:
Just as a sin offering, which is not totally consumed,
if one slaughtered it not for its sake, it is disqualified,
then a burnt offering, which is totally consumed,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֶּן עַזַּאי בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 17 defeats the 'הוּא' approach, the גמרא replaces it with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: a קל וחומר instead of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן עזאי learns his rule from the word 'הוּא' by the עולה
steps.terutzMaskana: בן עזאי is said to learn it from a קל וחומר from חטאת, so the אשם's 'הוּא' is no longer a problem. This proposal is itself challenged in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The גמרא proposes a קל וחומר from חטאת as בן עזאי's source. Step 19 rejects it.

steps.title: A sin offering is special because it atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from חטאת: maybe חטאת is strict only because it brings כפרה for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a sin offering? It is different because it atones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר from Step 18. It points out that חטאת has a special quality that עולה lacks, so you cannot learn עולה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from one case to another only works if the first case has no extra strict feature. חטאת atones for a specific sin, so maybe that is the reason it is פסול שלא לשמה. An עולה is not brought for such a sin, so the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? It is the standard opening for showing that the source case has something special.
It atones. A חטאת brings forgiveness for a specific sin.
Atonement

phrases.english: What about a sin offering? It is different, since it atones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר from חטאת proposed in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from חטאת to עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case (חטאת) has a stricter quality, atonement, that the target case (עולה) lacks. That quality may be the real reason for the פסול.

steps.title: The פסח proves the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings פסח, which does not atone, yet is still פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסח will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule by bringing a second example, the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח is not brought to atone for a sin, yet it is still פסול שלא לשמה. That shows atonement is not the reason for the פסול. So the challenge from Step 19 is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the Paschal offering
Will prove. It brings a case that breaks the objection.

phrases.english: The Paschal offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: Meaning: פסח doesn't atone, yet it's still פסול שלא לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by showing a case without atonement that is still פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Atonement is the reason חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח has no atonement and is still פסול, so atonement is not the reason.

steps.title: The פסח is special because of its fixed time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from פסח: maybe פסח is strict only because it has a fixed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the פסח? It is different because its time is fixed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the new proof. פסח also has a special quality that עולה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח can only be brought at a set time, on ערב פסח. Maybe that fixed time is what makes it פסול שלא לשמה. An עולה has no fixed time, so you cannot learn it from פסח either.

keyTerms.meaning: What about the פסח? It is special.
Its time
Fixed, set

phrases.english: What about the Paschal offering? It is different, since its time is fixed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the counter-example from פסח given in Step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח has a stricter feature, a fixed time, that עולה lacks. That feature may be the real reason for the פסול.

steps.title: The sin offering proves the point back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חטאת has no fixed time, yet is still פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sin offering will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to חטאת to answer the challenge against פסח. This also sets up the final step, where the two cases are joined together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת has no fixed time, yet it is still פסול שלא לשמה. So a fixed time cannot be the reason. Now each example answers the challenge against the other one.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Will prove (the feminine form, since חטאת is feminine)
Invalid

phrases.english: The sin offering will prove it.
phrases.notes: Meaning: חטאת has no set time, yet it's still פסול שלא לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by pointing to חטאת, which has no fixed time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fixed time is the reason פסח is פסול שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: חטאת has no fixed time and is still פסול, so a fixed time is not the reason.

steps.title: Learning עולה from what חטאת and פסח share
steps.stepSummary: Each case has its own special feature, so the rule must come from what they share. Both are קדשים and are פסול שלא לשמה, so עולה is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they are קדשים, and if they are slaughtered not for their own sake they are invalid. So too I will include עולה: it is קדשים, and if it is slaughtered not for its own sake it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the back-and-forth with a הצד השוה. It learns the rule for עולה from the feature that both חטאת and פסח share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת's special feature (atonement) is missing in פסח, and פסח's special feature (fixed time) is missing in חטאת. So neither special feature can be the reason for the פסול. The only thing left is that both are קדשים, and עולה is also קדשים, so it too is פסול שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has come back around to the start
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that one
The shared feature. It is a way of learning a rule from what two cases have in common.
Sacred offerings
Not for their own sake, meaning slaughtered with the wrong offering in mind

steps.whatToRemember: Since חטאת alone and פסח alone each get knocked down, the גמרא tries a הצד השוה from both together, based on their being קדשים. The next step challenges this too.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think חטאת or פסח alone proves the rule. Each one alone gets knocked down, so the גמרא tries joining them through what they share. Even this combined proof is challenged in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's third try at a source for בן עזאי, after the 'הוּא' approach and the plain קל וחומר both ran into problems. It too is challenged in the next step.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around;
the feature of this one is not like the feature of that one,
and the feature of that one is not like the feature of this one;
the shared feature between them –
is that they are sacred offerings,
and if one slaughtered them not for their own sake, it is invalid;
so too I will include a burnt offering –
since it is a sacred offering,
and if one slaughtered it not for its own sake, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין; לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two counter-examples of Steps 20 and 22 into a הצד השוה proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A הצד השוה from חטאת and פסח is proposed as the source for עולה. Step 24 rejects it.

steps.title: Both cases share a link to כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the צד השוה proof. Both חטאת and פסח are linked to כרת, so maybe that shared feature is why they are strict, and עולה has no such link.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about what they have in common? They both have a connection to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of step 23. It finds a second feature that חטאת and פסח both share but עולה does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה proof only works if the shared feature we use, being קדשים, is the only thing the two cases have in common. Here the גמרא points out that חטאת and פסח also share a link to כרת: a חטאת comes for a sin that brings כרת when done on purpose, and someone who skips the פסח is חייב כרת. Since עולה has no link to כרת, maybe its law is more lenient, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The common feature: a way of learning a law from two cases by what they share
A connection to the punishment of כרת
Spiritual 'cutting off,' a severe punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: The קשיא does not say חטאת and פסח both bring כרת in the same way. The חטאת atones for a כרת sin, while not bringing the פסח is itself a כרת sin. Either way, both are linked to כרת.

phrases.english: What is special about their common feature?
That they have an element of כרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the צד השוה conclusion of step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה proof from חטאת and פסח to עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two sources share a second strict feature, a link to כרת, that עולה does not have. So the strictness may come from that feature and not from simply being קדשים.

steps.title: The answer begins with בן עזאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its reply to the כרת challenge: 'As for בן עזאי...' It is about to explain how בן עזאי himself derives his rule. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening word of the answer. The גמרא is setting up its reply by naming בן עזאי, and the rest of his teaching comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the צד השוה proof was knocked down, the גמרא still needs to explain where בן עזאי gets his rule that an עולה is פסול שלא לשמה. It opens with his name to introduce his actual derivation, which appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where we hear how בן עזאי learns his rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the כרת challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Begins explaining בן עזאי's own derivation in place of the rejected צד השוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a further source, עולה might not be פסול שלא לשמה, since it lacks any link to כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come: בן עזאי's teaching will supply the source for עולה.
